requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1
requirements.summary: useradd -m -s /bin/bash appworker succeeded and id appworker resolved to uid=1000(appworker) gid=1000(appworker) both before and after the reboot, confirming the account was created and persisted.

requirements.requirement: Limit appworker login sessions to 8,192 open files (nofile)
requirements.summary: /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf sets soft/hard nofile 8192, pam_limits.so is confirmed active in /etc/pam.d/login, and a real login shell (sudo -u appworker -i bash -lc) reports ulimit -n=8192 both pre- and post-reboot.

requirements.requirement: Limit appworker login sessions to 256 processes (nproc)
requirements.summary: limits.d/appworker.conf sets soft/hard nproc 256; a real bash login session (not the initial sh session, which lacked ulimit -u support) confirms ulimit -u=256 both before and after reboot.

overall_summary: The executor created the appworker account and configured /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf with nofile=8192 and nproc=256, verified via real login shells enforcing pam_limits both before and after a single acknowledged reboot on node1. The provider-wide restart-evidence protocol was also satisfied for node1: a healthy pre-restart baseline (boot_id f9bf293d...), a returned reboot acknowledgement, a differing post-restart boot_id (38b52693...) matching the fixed after-executor snapshot, and recovered account/limits state were all directly observed.
limitations: The single-node topology means the restart protocol was only exercised on node1; no cross-node comparison was possible or needed.

The first ulimit -u check used sh instead of bash and failed with an unrelated shell syntax error, requiring a follow-up command to get a valid nproc reading; this did not affect the final verified outcome.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map directly to task outcomes or the mandated restart-evidence protocol: user creation, limits.conf write, a single acknowledged reboot to demonstrate persistence, and verification reads. No abandoned files, failed services, unnecessary mutations, or weakened security controls were observed. The initial sh-based ulimit -u probe failed harmlessly (illegal option) and was immediately corrected with a bash login shell — a diagnostic retry, not a mutation. Lifecycle diff shows only expected boot-identity-derived churn (systemd-private tmp dirs, ephemeral socket PIDs), no residue attributable to executor error.
